name: a step whose detail carries a bidirectional mark
why: A bidirectional mark has no width of its own and reorders the neutral text that follows it, so a fact can read on the page as one claim and be stored in the snapshot as another -- the same harm as a direction override, under another Unicode heading. It is outside the characters a fact may carry: letters, marks, numbers, punctuation, symbols and ordinary spaces, and nothing invisible by default (decided on #27, 28 Oct 2026).
